data.claim: Command gates, per-project pipelines, reviewers, rules and promotion already carry the generic workflow; twelve specific gaps (IaC kind, plan-bound apply approval, cloud sandbox lifecycle, policy records, module kind, schema check, finding ingest, supply-chain verification, drift jobs, CI-platform and forge adapters, deployment records, compliance evidence) are not planned.
data.falsifier: A queue search finds planned tasks that already cover a listed gap, or a project of this kind cannot run its gates as command gates today.
data.mechanism: QUESTION: can ddflow, with what exists and what is planned, manage projects whose product is infrastructure as code (Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi, CDK, Ansible, Helm, Kustomize, Packer, Crossplane, Bicep, CloudFormation), DevOps and DevSecOps work, and the CI/CD pipelines of GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Gitea and Azure DevOps? WHAT ALREADY WORKS TODAY: the gate pipeline is per-project data and any command can be a command gate (terraform fmt/validate/test, tflint, checkov, conftest, actionlint run as gates today); rules, decisions, lessons, goals engine (planned P-goals), leases and worktrees isolate agents, cross-family reviewers (Kimi, DeepSeek) review diffs, the codeguide and context7 companions serve standards and docs, ddflow promote tracks environment branches and recorded deploy shas, forge adapters (infra/forge.py) drive GitHub through gh and GitLab through glab for PR state, a ci gate runs the project's CI command set locally (D-ci-parity). Unavailable tools are recorded unavailable, never passed. WHAT IS PLANNED AND HELPS: SC-catalogue/SC-data-more (stack probe with an IaC data wave, data only), TF-flows-system pipeline-validate and TF-cadence (per-commit, per-PR, nightly, post-deploy sets), TD-emulation/TD-pins/TD-lease (containers, version pins and image digests, leases for scarce equipment), SE-ask-core approvals with content digests, SE-waiver, AG-deps-guard (dependencies agents add), P-safeguards (cards, consult action for context7/codeguide), P-schedule.watch, B-gap-checks-publish (gate state as a forge check), CP-intake (webhook intake), P-org-config (corporate policy layers), P-goals (measurable goals). THE WEB (2026): the IaC test pyramid is static (fmt, validate, tflint, checkov/trivy/tfsec/kics) about 70 percent, module-level plan and terraform test with mocks about 25 percent, apply-in-sandbox (Terratest) and nightly end-to-end about 5 percent; policy as code is OPA/Conftest or Sentinel run on the JSON plan (terraform show -json), first in warn mode then enforcing after two clean sprints; plan and apply are separated and the approved plan is what is applied (Atlantis, Spacelift, env0, HCP Terraform), with state locking and scheduled drift detection (plan -detailed-exitcode); modules are versioned by semver where removed variables, renamed outputs and changed resource types are breaking, published by git tag to a registry, documented by terraform-docs; HashiCorp ships a Terraform MCP server (registry search, provider docs, workspaces) and the TerraFormer paper (2026-01) and field reports show models hallucinate resource types and attributes, which a provider-schema check catches deterministically; DevSecOps means OIDC short-lived cloud credentials instead of static keys, SLSA provenance, Sigstore/cosign signatures, SBOMs, SARIF findings, secret scanning, and gates fast enough that nobody routes around them; pipelines are code with their own linters (actionlint, GitLab CI Lint API, the Jenkins declarative linter, Azure Pipelines validation, Gitea/Forgejo Actions on act_runner) and local runners (act, gitlab-ci-local). GAPS: (1) no first-class IaC stack kind with per-tool gate roles, tool and provider version pins and lock-file checks; (2) no plan record bound to commit, variables and workspace, so no 'apply only the plan that was approved' gate and no production-apply guard for agents; (3) no cloud sandbox lifecycle (TTL, guaranteed teardown, cost cap, orphan sweep, OIDC credentials) beyond local containers; (4) no policy-as-code record kind with enforce ramp and waivers with expiry mapped to executable bundles; (5) no module record kind (build, consume, semver by contract diff, registry provenance, lock hashes); (6) no provider-schema hallucination check and no registered Terraform MCP companion; (7) no SARIF/plan-JSON finding ingest with triage; (8) no provenance, signature and SBOM verification gate for images and modules; (9) no scheduled drift detection filing work; (10) forge support is GitHub and GitLab only (no Gitea/Forgejo, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket) and there is no CI-platform adapter for detect, lint, local run, status and logs, nor pipeline generation from ddflow's own gates with drift check; (11) no deployment, environment and release record beyond branch promotion (artifact digest, rollback plan, freeze windows, change-ticket link, post-deploy gates); (12) no compliance evidence pack mapping controls to gates.

data.question: Can ddflow's current and planned features manage infrastructure-as-code, DevOps and DevSecOps projects and the CI/CD pipelines of GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Gitea and Azure DevOps, and what is missing?

data.claim: The planned constellation covers the version pair, change request and drift ideas, but eleven specifics for infrastructure siblings (roles, environment contract adapters, artifact handoff, sibling proposals, deploy-aware matrix, plan impact, coordinated release, contract test, three-way drift, lifecycle, on-prem) are not planned.
data.falsifier: A read of CN-roles, CN-manifest, CN-matrix and CN-libs shows they already model environments, deployments or infrastructure contracts.
data.mechanism: QUESTION: an application project and a sister project that holds the pipelines and infrastructure as code for it (cloud or on-prem): how do they coordinate so ddflow keeps both in sync? WHAT THE CONSTELLATION PLANS (P-constellation, D-constellation): a manifest of member projects with roles, spec records with format adapters (OpenAPI, protobuf, ASN.1, YANG, DBC, register maps), digest-pinned cross-project references, consumer edges and an impact query, change requests with a consumer state machine (pending, acknowledged, adopting, adopted, not_affected), baselines, a compatibility matrix with a can-i-release gate, a breaking-change gate classified by the adapter's checker, shared library registry (CN-libs) with a bump workflow that never edits another project's lockfile, a read-only sibling mirror, optional push nudge (CN-dispatch), a scheduled drift audit, topologies single repo, monorepo, polyrepo, submodule umbrella. THE WEB: a typical split is an app repo whose CI builds the image and a separate GitOps config repo that Argo CD or Flux watches (separate so the CD system does not trigger itself); promotion is a pull request that bumps an image tag or module version per environment (separate directories, branches, repos, or tag promotion); Flux image automation or Kargo promotion tasks do it automatically; versions follow semver with scope prefixes; the contract between the two is inputs and outputs of modules, Helm values and schema, manifests, environment variables, ports and health endpoints; a Pact-style can-i-deploy asks whether this version pair is verified together. WHAT FITS TODAY: infra and app can be two constellation members; CN-matrix and the can-i-release gate express version pairs; CN-cr carries change requests; ddflow promote and CN-libs bump workflows cover tags. GAPS: (1) no member roles for app, infra, gitops-config, module-library and pipeline-library, and no gitops-config topology; (2) no environment contract kind with adapters for Terraform variables and outputs, Helm values schema, Kubernetes manifests (kubeconform), config and environment-variable schemas, so what the app NEEDS from the infrastructure and what the infrastructure PROVIDES is not machine-checked; (3) no artifact handoff record (image digest, chart or module version, SBOM, provenance) that the infra project consumes by digest; (4) no way to open a proposal in the sibling repository through the forge with a change request attached; (5) the matrix is release-time, not deploy-aware: no rows per environment from deployment records and no can-i-deploy gate before an apply or promotion; (6) no plan-impact analysis: an infra plan diff that changes an output the app uses, or an app change that adds an environment variable, must raise a change request in the other project; (7) no coordinated release workflow (ordering, expand and contract, shared rollback, freeze windows); (8) no environment contract test against terraform output or rendered manifests; (9) no three-way drift audit (declared in the infra repo, deployed per deployment records and cloud reads, running version and health); (10) no lifecycle workflows for decommission, rename, secret rotation (references only) and deprecation notices; (11) no on-prem and air-gapped support (Ansible inventories, Packer images, offline registry and provider mirrors, hardware leases); (12) pipeline libraries (GitHub reusable workflows, GitLab includes, Jenkins shared libraries, Azure templates) are not versioned or pinned like code libraries.

N1="""QUESTION: can ddflow, with what exists and what is planned, manage projects whose product is infrastructure as code (Terraform, OpenTofu, Pulumi, CDK, Ansible, Helm, Kustomize, Packer, Crossplane, Bicep, CloudFormation), DevOps and DevSecOps work, and the CI/CD pipelines of GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Gitea and Azure DevOps? WHAT ALREADY WORKS TODAY: the gate pipeline is per-project data and any command can be a command gate (terraform fmt/validate/test, tflint, checkov, conftest, actionlint run as gates today); rules, decisions, lessons, goals engine (planned P-goals), leases and worktrees isolate agents, cross-family reviewers (Kimi, DeepSeek) review diffs, the codeguide and context7 companions serve standards and docs, ddflow promote tracks environment branches and recorded deploy shas, forge adapters (infra/forge.py) drive GitHub through gh and GitLab through glab for PR state, a ci gate runs the project's CI command set locally (D-ci-parity). Unavailable tools are recorded unavailable, never passed. WHAT IS PLANNED AND HELPS: SC-catalogue/SC-data-more (stack probe with an IaC data wave, data only), TF-flows-system pipeline-validate and TF-cadence (per-commit, per-PR, nightly, post-deploy sets), TD-emulation/TD-pins/TD-lease (containers, version pins and image digests, leases for scarce equipment), SE-ask-core approvals with content digests, SE-waiver, AG-deps-guard (dependencies agents add), P-safeguards (cards, consult action for context7/codeguide), P-schedule.watch, B-gap-checks-publish (gate state as a forge check), CP-intake (webhook intake), P-org-config (corporate policy layers), P-goals (measurable goals). THE WEB (2026): the IaC test pyramid is static (fmt, validate, tflint, checkov/trivy/tfsec/kics) about 70 percent, module-level plan and terraform test with mocks about 25 percent, apply-in-sandbox (Terratest) and nightly end-to-end about 5 percent; policy as code is OPA/Conftest or Sentinel run on the JSON plan (terraform show -json), first in warn mode then enforcing after two clean sprints; plan and apply are separated and the approved plan is what is applied (Atlantis, Spacelift, env0, HCP Terraform), with state locking and scheduled drift detection (plan -detailed-exitcode); modules are versioned by semver where removed variables, renamed outputs and changed resource types are breaking, published by git tag to a registry, documented by terraform-docs; HashiCorp ships a Terraform MCP server (registry search, provider docs, workspaces) and the TerraFormer paper (2026-01) and field reports show models hallucinate resource types and attributes, which a provider-schema check catches deterministically; DevSecOps means OIDC short-lived cloud credentials instead of static keys, SLSA provenance, Sigstore/cosign signatures, SBOMs, SARIF findings, secret scanning, and gates fast enough that nobody routes around them; pipelines are code with their own linters (actionlint, GitLab CI Lint API, the Jenkins declarative linter, Azure Pipelines validation, Gitea/Forgejo Actions on act_runner) and local runners (act, gitlab-ci-local). GAPS: (1) no first-class IaC stack kind with per-tool gate roles, tool and provider version pins and lock-file checks; (2) no plan record bound to commit, variables and workspace, so no 'apply only the plan that was approved' gate and no production-apply guard for agents; (3) no cloud sandbox lifecycle (TTL, guaranteed teardown, cost cap, orphan sweep, OIDC credentials) beyond local containers; (4) no policy-as-code record kind with enforce ramp and waivers with expiry mapped to executable bundles; (5) no module record kind (build, consume, semver by contract diff, registry provenance, lock hashes); (6) no provider-schema hallucination check and no registered Terraform MCP companion; (7) no SARIF/plan-JSON finding ingest with triage; (8) no provenance, signature and SBOM verification gate for images and modules; (9) no scheduled drift detection filing work; (10) forge support is GitHub and GitLab only (no Gitea/Forgejo, Azure DevOps, Bitbucket) and there is no CI-platform adapter for detect, lint, local run, status and logs, nor pipeline generation from ddflow's own gates with drift check; (11) no deployment, environment and release record beyond branch promotion (artifact digest, rollback plan, freeze windows, change-ticket link, post-deploy gates); (12) no compliance evidence pack mapping controls to gates."""
run(["research","add","--new","--id","R-iac-devops","--question","Can ddflow's current and planned features manage infrastructure-as-code, DevOps and DevSecOps projects and the CI/CD pipelines of GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins, Gitea and Azure DevOps, and what is missing?","--claim","Command gates, per-project pipelines, reviewers, rules and promotion already carry the generic workflow; twelve specific gaps (IaC kind, plan-bound apply approval, cloud sandbox lifecycle, policy records, module kind, schema check, finding ingest, supply-chain verification, drift jobs, CI-platform and forge adapters, deployment records, compliance evidence) are not planned.","--mechanism",N1,"--falsifier","A queue search finds planned tasks that already cover a listed gap, or a project of this kind cannot run its gates as command gates today.","--probe","queue grep for terraform, iac, pipeline, deploy, policy, drift, sandbox, gitea, azure, jenkins, sarif, sbom, slsa; read TF-flows-system, SC-data-more, TD-emulation, B-gap-checks-publish, CN-matrix, infra/forge.py; ddflow promote --help; ddflow companions","--probe-output","terraform/opentofu/pulumi/ansible/helm: 0 tasks; iac: SC-data-more (data only); gitea/azure devops/jenkins/bitbucket: 0; forge adapters: GitHub and GitLab only; promote: add/deployed/status by branch; sarif/slsa/sbom/cosign: 0 (AG-deps-guard covers app dependencies only)","--verdict","CONFIRMED","--sources","https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-02-23-how-to-implement-infrastructure-as-code-testing-pyramid-with-terraform/view; https://kokil.com.np/blog/policy-as-code-with-opa-and-conftest; https://codex.danielvaughan.com/2026/06/10/codex-cli-terraform-infrastructure-as-code-mcp-server-terrashark-pulumi-agent-skills/; https://www.env0.com/frameworks/atlantis-for-terraform-how-it-works-limitations-better-alternatives; https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-01-30-terraform-module-versioning/view; https://cloudaware.com/blog/zero-trust-devsecops/"])
N2="""QUESTION: an application project and a sister project that holds the pipelines and infrastructure as code for it (cloud or on-prem): how do they coordinate so ddflow keeps both in sync? WHAT THE CONSTELLATION PLANS (P-constellation, D-constellation): a manifest of member projects with roles, spec records with format adapters (OpenAPI, protobuf, ASN.1, YANG, DBC, register maps), digest-pinned cross-project references, consumer edges and an impact query, change requests with a consumer state machine (pending, acknowledged, adopting, adopted, not_affected), baselines, a compatibility matrix with a can-i-release gate, a breaking-change gate classified by the adapter's checker, shared library registry (CN-libs) with a bump workflow that never edits another project's lockfile, a read-only sibling mirror, optional push nudge (CN-dispatch), a scheduled drift audit, topologies single repo, monorepo, polyrepo, submodule umbrella. THE WEB: a typical split is an app repo whose CI builds the image and a separate GitOps config repo that Argo CD or Flux watches (separate so the CD system does not trigger itself); promotion is a pull request that bumps an image tag or module version per environment (separate directories, branches, repos, or tag promotion); Flux image automation or Kargo promotion tasks do it automatically; versions follow semver with scope prefixes; the contract between the two is inputs and outputs of modules, Helm values and schema, manifests, environment variables, ports and health endpoints; a Pact-style can-i-deploy asks whether this version pair is verified together. WHAT FITS TODAY: infra and app can be two constellation members; CN-matrix and the can-i-release gate express version pairs; CN-cr carries change requests; ddflow promote and CN-libs bump workflows cover tags. GAPS: (1) no member roles for app, infra, gitops-config, module-library and pipeline-library, and no gitops-config topology; (2) no environment contract kind with adapters for Terraform variables and outputs, Helm values schema, Kubernetes manifests (kubeconform), config and environment-variable schemas, so what the app NEEDS from the infrastructure and what the infrastructure PROVIDES is not machine-checked; (3) no artifact handoff record (image digest, chart or module version, SBOM, provenance) that the infra project consumes by digest; (4) no way to open a proposal in the sibling repository through the forge with a change request attached; (5) the matrix is release-time, not deploy-aware: no rows per environment from deployment records and no can-i-deploy gate before an apply or promotion; (6) no plan-impact analysis: an infra plan diff that changes an output the app uses, or an app change that adds an environment variable, must raise a change request in the other project; (7) no coordinated release workflow (ordering, expand and contract, shared rollback, freeze windows); (8) no environment contract test against terraform output or rendered manifests; (9) no three-way drift audit (declared in the infra repo, deployed per deployment records and cloud reads, running version and health); (10) no lifecycle workflows for decommission, rename, secret rotation (references only) and deprecation notices; (11) no on-prem and air-gapped support (Ansible inventories, Packer images, offline registry and provider mirrors, hardware leases); (12) pipeline libraries (GitHub reusable workflows, GitLab includes, Jenkins shared libraries, Azure templates) are not versioned or pinned like code libraries."""
run(["research","add","--new","--id","R-app-infra-sync","--question","How can an application project and its sister pipelines-and-infrastructure project coordinate, cooperate and be kept in sync by ddflow, and what does the planned constellation miss for that?","--claim","The planned constellation covers the version pair, change request and drift ideas, but eleven specifics for infrastructure siblings (roles, environment contract adapters, artifact handoff, sibling proposals, deploy-aware matrix, plan impact, coordinated release, contract test, three-way drift, lifecycle, on-prem) are not planned.","--mechanism",N2,"--falsifier","A read of CN-roles, CN-manifest, CN-matrix and CN-libs shows they already model environments, deployments or infrastructure contracts.","--probe","read CN-manifest, CN-matrix, CN-libs, CN-workflows, CN-dispatch, CN-adapter-* task bodies; ddflow promote --help; queue grep for environment, deployment, gitops, helm, contract","--probe-output","adapter groups: openapi, protobuf, asn1, yang/wsdl, embedded (dbc, arxml, ip-xact); no terraform, helm, kubernetes or env-schema adapter; matrix is spec@digest per release; no environment or deployment record; promote tracks branches only","--verdict","CONFIRMED","--sources","https://semaphore.io/blog/how-to-integrate-ci-cd-with-gitops-tools-like-argo-cd-or-flux; https://oneuptime.com/blog/post/2026-02-26-argocd-environment-promotion/view; https://mattias.engineer/blog/2023/gitops-environment-promotion/; https://github.com/argoproj/argo-cd/discussions/5667"])

(PH1,"IA-plan-apply","Plan record and apply gate: the approved plan digest is the only thing that may be applied","SE-ask-core,TF-record,IA-stack",["ddflow/services/iac/plan*.py","tests/test_iac_plan_apply.py"],"68","A plan is evidence: plan JSON hashed and bound to the commit, variables, workspace and tool versions, expiring after a knob; an apply gate refuses anything but the digest a person (or, per the agreed agent rights, a rule) approved through the approvals engine; production apply by an agent is refused by default; state locking and a failed apply are recorded, not retried silently; no state file or secret is ever stored in the log (references and digests only)."),

(PH1,"IA-policy","Policy-as-code records: OPA/Conftest, Sentinel, Kyverno and scanner custom rules as versioned bundles with an enforce ramp and expiring waivers","SE-waiver,B-pipe-model,B-org-layers,IA-stack",["ddflow/services/iac/policy*.py","tests/test_iac_policy.py"],"69","A corporate policy is a record (owner, version, bundle source and digest, scope, severity) that maps onto the guidance pipeline effects; the shipped ramp is warn-only for N clean runs then blocking; a waiver is one scoped, reasoned, expiring record through the approvals engine; the org layer (P-org-config) distributes policies; results are findings (IA-sarif), never a bare exit code."),

(PH1,"IA-supply-chain","Supply-chain gate: signatures, provenance and SBOM verified for images and modules, digests pinned","AG-deps-guard,TD-pins,IA-decide",["ddflow/services/iac/supplychain*.py","tests/test_iac_supplychain.py"],"70","Images and modules referenced by the IaC must be pinned by digest or lock hash; cosign signatures and SLSA provenance are verified where the producer publishes them (level per the decision); an SBOM is attached to the artifact record; an unverifiable artifact is unavailable or flagged by policy, never passed; extends the dependency guard of AG-deps-guard to infrastructure artifacts."),

fields.body: Decision D-company-workflows (operator 2026-10-15, verbatim: 'Keep as a rule, that the user or company policies should be able to change anything with config, cli, mcp command, or prompt, to allow companies or projects to have specific and individual workflows'). Extends r-everything-configurable and D-universal-principles. When you add or change a feature: (1) nothing ddflow ships is a fixed policy: every workflow, pipeline, gate, role, rule, template, prompt, default, threshold and shipped record is a default that a USER or a COMPANY policy can change, per company and per project, by config file, CLI, MCP command or a plain prompt, with no code change; (2) layers are system, company (organisation config, P-org-config), project, user; a company may mark keys non-overridable below it (floors) and a project may tighten but not loosen a floor; (3) a feature that cannot be adapted this way is not done: the standards gate and reviewers check that the new behaviour has a knob or an overridable record, a way to turn it off or replace it, and tests that run with the override; (4) every change is logged and restorable from the log (config.changed, record events); (5) company defaults arrive through the org bundle and are reviewable, diffable and revertible; (6) shipped examples (workflow packs, policies, pipelines) are copied, never edited in place, so an upgrade does not overwrite a customisation.

data.summary: pytest keeps only the last 3 numbered base-temp directories per user (/tmp/pytest-of-<user>/pytest-N) and each new session removes older ones. ddflow's agents run full suites and the pre-push hook at the same time, so a LIVE session's directory is deleted by a newer session's startup. Observed 2026-10-15 in the operator's pre-push run (a clean 11763 passed, 1 error): test_contested_claim_surface setup failed 'git clone ... fatal: failed to copy file to .../pytest-15588/popen-gw35/.../b/.git/objects/maintenance.lock: No such file or directory'; the same test passes alone (11 passed). 14 pytest processes were running at that moment (five fleet agents). Fix direction: give every session its own base temp (tests/conftest.py pytest_configure sets --basetemp to a per-process unique directory unless one is given, removed at session finish) and set tmp_path_retention_count/policy so nothing else prunes it; the pre-push hook and ddflow gate runs inherit it. Regression test: start two pytest sessions at once with a retention of 1 and assert the first keeps its directory.

data.body: CORRECTED 2026-10-15. The first diagnosis (concurrent pytest sessions prune each other's tmp dirs) is NOT supported: a live session's directory is protected by pytest's lock file, and an experiment with one long session and six newer ones kept it. The single occurrence was a setup error in a test that pushes into a bare remote and clones it: 'fatal: failed to copy file to .../b/.git/objects/maintenance.lock: No such file or directory' (11763 passed, 1 error; the test passes alone). Git's local clone copies the remote's objects/ directory file by file, and auto-maintenance (git maintenance run --auto, gc --auto) started by the push takes objects/maintenance.lock while it runs: a lock that disappears between the listing and the copy fails the clone. UNPROVEN: 150 push-and-clone iterations under 8 busy loops did not reproduce it. Fix (mitigation): the suite switches git auto-maintenance off for every git process (tests/_gitquiet.py, applied in tests/conftest.py via GIT_CONFIG_COUNT). Regression test: tests/test_git_quiet_env.py (fails on the unfixed conftest). If the setup error ever recurs with maintenance off, the cause is something else: capture ls of the tmp dir at failure.

The new tests fail on the unfixed conftest (gc.auto unset).

data.body:
Fixes bug B9eeecd134c: The scheduler lists 'X is abandoned' as the reason a task is blocked but never marks the dependent as permanently stuck, and doctor is silent. 67 tasks were blocked this way on 2026-10-15 (decide tasks settled by abandon as a decision), 9 by nothing else. Fix: doctor reports a needs edge to an abandoned (not done) item with the command that drops it, and ddflow abandon of an item others need warns and lists the dependents (offering to drop the edges or re-point them). Regression test: a task needing an abandoned task is reported by doctor and abandon warns.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B9eeecd134c --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B9eeecd134c --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B9eeecd134c: A needs edge to an abandoned item blocks the dependent forever and nothing reports it as stuck

data.how: Before abandoning a decide task, list its dependents (ddflow show of the dependents, or the next output) and drop the edge; doctor will report such an edge once B9eeecd134c is fixed.
data.rule: Do not put a decide task in another task's needs; the decision record governs by globs. If one is there, drop the edge with ddflow update --needs once the decision is recorded.
data.title: A task that needs a decide task is stuck for good once the decide task is abandoned as a decision
data.why: ddflow treats an abandoned prerequisite as unsatisfied and the convention settles a decide task by abandoning it. 67 tasks waited forever on 2026-10-15 (9 on nothing else); the brief said 'X is abandoned' but nothing called it stuck.

data.decision:
[D-skills-spec-native] A ddflow-managed skill is a spec-compliant directory (SKILL.md + optional scripts/ references/ assets/) that any agent reads unchanged. ddflow-specific data (digest, source, version, sync state) lives in the event log and .ddflow/skills.lock, or in the spec's free-form metadata map, never in new frontmatter fields.

[D-skills-canonical-store] Default canonical store is .agents/skills/ (the cross-client convention); [skills].canonical can name another. 'ddflow skill sync' makes symlinks (default), copies, or generated files in each enabled agent's directory, marks what it manages, never overwrites a skill it did not create, and reports drift. Skills already in an agent directory are adopted, not moved, until the operator asks.

[D-skills-operator-answers] Decided by the operator 2026-10-03: (1) YAML parsing uses PyYAML with a colon-quote retry (add it as a dependency). (2) Skill sync defaults to COPY with drift detection against a managed sidecar; symlink is opt-in. (3) Install/pin use skills-lock.json at the repo root, compatible with the vercel format, with ddflow-namespaced fields (ref, commit, treeSha, hashAlgo, files) and a precisely defined full sha256 tree digest. (4) skill doctor: errors fail the exit code (1), warnings are advisory, and the report always says static checks only. (5) ddflow writes skills inside the repo only; user-level dirs ([REDACTED:path], [REDACTED:path]) are read-only for inventory unless [skills].user_level = true and an explicit command. (6) Agent-authored skills need a recorded human acknowledgement before they sync. (7) ddflow's invariants (brief first, claim before edit, the four enforced rules) stay in always-on context; skills carry only conditional procedures (onboard, review triage, verify, import, the driver), and an A/B adherence eval (B-skills-adherence-eval) precedes moving any instruction. (8) A Claude Code plugin named ddflow ships LAST, after the pack and sync are proven. DEFAULTS applied unless the operator objects (not asked): lint strictness is per-agent lenient (extras tolerated by agents are warnings 'rejected by skills-ref', not errors); names are ASCII on 'skill new' and NFKC-normalised on read; skills with scripts/, hooks, .mcp.json or bare Bash allowed-tools are installable only with a recorded approval; generated .mdc/Cline/AGENTS.md translations are committed with a do-not-edit banner; rules and skills stay separate record types with one shared 'what applies' view; MCP skill serving (SEP-2640) is opt-in later.

OPERATOR 2026-10-15 (AskUserQuestion), settling the conflict between D-skills-canonical-store (symlinks by default) and D-skills-operator-answers (copy): COPY by default, with drift detection; symlinks are an opt-in knob for a project. Everything else in this record stands.

data.decision:
CURRENT RULE (the operator's D-roadmap-review item 2, 2026-10-14, quoted as recorded): (2) UPGRADE: session start only prints the one-line notice ([upgrade].auto=check); on MCP connect the agent proposes the upgrade and the operator consents; container start applies safe categories only, and only when [upgrade].auto is safe.

The four superseded records follow as recorded. Where one of them says otherwise on writes (D-self-upgrade (5) and D-self-upgrade-defaults let container or MCP start apply safe categories under [upgrade].on_start = safe; D-upgrade-auto-check makes safe an opt-in), the rule above governs. Release check, self-upgrade command, consent and rollback, and orchestrate-and-monitor from D-self-upgrade stand as recorded. Other upgrade records (D-upgrade-event-kinds, D-upgrade-backups, D-upgrade-config-changes, D-upgrade-manifest-lint, D-upgrade-skew-guard, D-dry-run-from-running-version, D-start-timeout-note) are not replaced.

[D-upgrade-auto-check] Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'Should [upgrade].auto ship as check - go for check'. [upgrade].auto = off|check|safe, shipped default check for every ddflow project: after ddflow is upgraded, the first session start on a machine prints one line (once per machine per version) such as 'ddflow upgraded 0.1.9 -> 0.1.10: run ddflow upgrade --plan' and writes nothing. safe (agents apply non-destructive categories) and off are configurable via config, CLI and MCP. Still OPEN in D-upgrade-model: skew guard default (operator proposed refuse-once with a recorded override flag), backup location, operator-only default changes, manifest lint. Accepted so far: D-upgrade-event-kinds.

[D-self-upgrade] Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'Make ddflow have a feature to periodically check for newer versions of ddflow, to propose to the operator upgrade of itself, to have self-upgrade cli command and capabilities which do migration and upgrades (in case of running docker it shall introduce check for upgrade and migration on container or mcp start and implement it while in container if the container version has been upgraded and database and other storage and config artifacts needs migration) need. The user should be capable to check, ask, request ddflow upgrade and orchestrate and monitor it'. Recorded design (defaults chosen by claude where the operator did not say; each is a knob the operator can change): (1) RELEASE CHECK: ddflow looks for a newer release of itself at most once per [upgrade].check_interval_h (default 24) from the package index it was installed from (and the image registry tag when running in a container); opportunistic at session start/brief/doctor, never a daemon, bounded by a short timeout, silent and harmless offline; the result is cached under .ddflow/local; it sends nothing but the request for the public version list (no project data, no telemetry). [upgrade].release_check = on|off (shipped default on, because the operator asked for periodic checks; off for air-gapped use; DDFLOW_NO_UPDATE_CHECK env). (2) PROPOSAL: a newer release is PROPOSED, never installed silently: one line in the session-start notice, brief, status and doctor ('ddflow X is available, you run Y: what changed + how to upgrade'), once per version per machine; an agent that sees it tells the operator. (3) SELF-UPGRADE: `ddflow upgrade --self` (CLI; MCP ddflow_upgrade action=self) detects how ddflow is installed (uv tool, pipx, pip in a venv, uvx/ephemeral, container image, source checkout) and either runs the right installer command or, where it cannot (container image, source checkout, read-only install), prints the exact command for the operator; installing new code is the operator's decision: an agent may run it only with the operator's recorded consent ([upgrade].self = ask|operator|auto, default ask); the old version is remembered so `ddflow upgrade --self --rollback` can reinstall it. (4) MIGRATION follows the install: after a self-upgrade, and on the first run of a new version, the project upgrade plan runs (ddflow upgrade --plan), and the categories allowed by [upgrade].auto are applied with a backup first; operator-set config needs confirmation (D-upgrade-config-changes). (5) CONTAINER / MCP START: when the server or the container starts, it compares its own version with the project's stamp (and the stores it mounts: log, index, local config, backups, hooks, instruction files); if the image is newer it runs the check and the safe migrations in the container before serving, reports what it did or what awaits the operator in the first brief, and never fails to start because of a pending migration (it serves, marks the plan pending and says so); if the image is OLDER than the project the skew guard applies (D-upgrade-skew-guard). [upgrade].on_start = check|safe|off (default safe for index/derived-store rebuilds and non-destructive categories; anything needing consent waits). (6) ORCHESTRATE AND MONITOR: the operator can ask at any time: ddflow upgrade --check (is there a newer release, is this project behind), --plan, --apply, --self, --status (what ran, what is pending, which agents/MCP servers still run the old version and must restart), --history, --restore; the same over MCP so the operator can ask an agent; every step is recorded as events so replay explains it; a running upgrade shows progress and can be resumed after an interruption (idempotent steps).

[D-self-upgrade-defaults] Operator 2026-10-03 (verbatim): 'I agree with your defaults'. Confirms the three defaults claude chose in D-self-upgrade: [upgrade].release_check = on (an outbound request for the public version list only, no project data; off or DDFLOW_NO_UPDATE_CHECK disables it; README states what is requested); [upgrade].self = ask (an agent installs new code only with the operator's recorded consent); [upgrade].on_start = safe (container/MCP start applies derived-store rebuilds and non-destructive backed-up categories; consent items wait). All remain configurable via config, CLI and MCP.

[D-upgrade-on-mcp-connect] Operator 2026-10-09: when the operator restarts and connects to the new MCP version it must detect the version difference by itself and start the upgrade, asking the operator for permission; nothing is applied without that consent.

OPERATOR 2026-10-15 (AskUserQuestion), confirming: container start applies safe categories ONLY when [upgrade].auto = safe; there is no separate [upgrade].on_start knob, and D-self-upgrade-defaults' on_start wording is superseded.

data.summary: Policy [enforce].generated_views = block refuses a commit of a rule file or DDFLOW.md with 'the event log it is rendered from has N change(s) the commit does not record' and compares the commit against the LIVE shards of the primary checkout. With several agents appending events all the time the check races: it took a loop of 'commit the shards in the primary, merge main into the worktree, commit' (and once copying the primary's shards into the worktree) to land one rule file. Fix: compare the view against the log AS COMMITTED in the commit's own history (or the events up to the view's own source events), not the working-tree shards other agents are writing. Regression test: stage a rule file while another process appends to a shard; the commit succeeds.

How could we prevent circular race conditions or locking of agents waiting each other for tasks that are not set dependent on each other?

data.body:
D-lease-hold-limit says hot-file locks are visible and time-limited: after hold_max_s a contended lease is breakable. grep finds no hold_max_s in the code (B-lease-hold-visibility, open, only warns). On 2026-10-15 three agents sat for 45+ minutes with current leases because a heartbeat loop renews an idle lease: liveness is not progress. Build: (1) a progress watermark per lease = the last event that is not a lease renewal (a commit, a gate record, a test job start, a note); (2) [lease].hold_max_s and idle_max_s: a lease that another ready item is waiting on (a recorded wait, see DX-lease-wait-cycle) and whose watermark is older than idle_max_s is marked yield-requested in brief/doctor/status, and after hold_max_s it is breakable by the waiter with `ddflow claim --break` (the holder's branch and work are kept; the holder gets the contested globs back only through the normal claim); (3) the holder sees the request in its next ddflow call. Related: B-lease-hold-visibility, DX-lease-wait-cycle. Regression test: an idle lease with a waiter is reported yield-requested and then breakable; an active lease never is.

data.title: Decided but not built: a contended lease held without progress becomes breakable (D-lease-hold-limit's hold_max_s), measured by PROGRESS not by heartbeats

data.body:
Hold-and-wait is the textbook deadlock condition and ddflow invites it: `ddflow update --globs` refuses a glob another lease holds, the agent keeps its current lease (often a hot file such as help.py) and polls, and the holder of the wanted glob does the same in the other direction. Fix: (1) `ddflow update --globs` and `ddflow claim` take an optional `--queue`: the refusal registers a waiting_on record (who, which globs, since when) and returns at once; (2) a waiter that cannot get the globs within [lease].wait_max_s must release the globs OTHER agents are waiting for (the scheduler names them) or report a cycle; (3) FIFO per glob so a waiter is not starved; (4) the mark expires with the waiter's lease. Related: DX-lease-wait-cycle (detect), DX-lease-progress-breakable (break). Regression test: two items that each want a glob the other holds are detected on the second refusal and one is told to release.

data.body:
The shared pin files (golden snapshots, setup transcript, README counts, result schemas) are needed only at merge time, but today every agent leases them from the moment it first needs a re-pin until it merges, so the wave serialised on whoever held them. Build on B-batch-integration: `ddflow merge --queue` marks an item ready (gates satisfied), the integrator (a ddflow command, run by the operator, a coordinator agent or a scheduled job, never required of the item's own agent) takes the queue head, merges main into the item's branch, regenerates the pins with `ddflow pins regenerate` (DX-pins-regenerate), runs ci, and merges; failures return the item with the reason. The pin files then need no exclusive lease. Related: B-batch-integration, DX-pins-regenerate, GitHub's merge queue (B-gap-checks-publish publishes the same verdict). Regression test: three items that each add a knob are merged in order by one integrator run with green pins and no manual step.

data.body:
On 2026-10-15 three agents deadlocked for 45+ minutes: fleet-docscmd needed help.py (leased by fleet-metrics), fleet-metrics waited for B-docs-check-command to finish because it held the golden snapshot, transcript and README, and fleet-logscale waited for the same item. Nothing was running, every lease was current (heartbeats renewing), and no ddflow command said anything: ddflow wait only sleeps on one item. Fix: record who waits for whom (ddflow wait --item and claim refusals leave a waiting_on mark with a TTL), have doctor and status report a cycle in the wait graph or a wait older than a knob with nothing running, naming the smallest release that breaks it (which glob to drop with ddflow update --globs), and have claim refusals print the holder's own wait. Regression test: three items with crossing globs produce the cycle report. CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, r-everything-configurable, r-company-workflows): every number a knob; files under 20 KB.

EXTENDED 2026-10-15 (design discussion): the detector reports a cycle in the wait-for graph (waiting_on marks from DX-no-hold-and-wait), picks a VICTIM (the waiter with the least progress, then the latest claim), asks it to yield the contested globs (yield-requested in brief/status, see DX-lease-progress-breakable) and prints the exact commands: `ddflow update <victim> --globs <without the contested ones>` for the victim and `ddflow wait --item` for the others. A coordinator or the lanes advisor (`ddflow lanes advise`) shows it without a human reading the log.

Can you set the rules, and also can you make sure that ddflow if it detects circular dependency or blockage which was undetected and not prevented in advance should refill the tasks with dependency on each other in order to prevent circular waiting and dependency and this way to force unblock?

Can you set the rules, and also can you make sure that ddflow if it detects circular dependency or blockage which was undetected and not prevented in advance should refill the tasks with dependency on each other in order to prevent circular waiting and dependency and this way to force unblock?

data.body:
Operator 2026-10-15 (D-lock-cycle-selfheal): if ddflow detects a circular dependency or blockage that was NOT declared and NOT prevented in advance, it must REFILL the tasks with dependencies on each other so the circular waiting cannot recur, and so force the unblock. Build on DX-lease-wait-cycle (detection: wait-for graph from the waiting_on marks of DX-no-hold-and-wait) and DX-lease-progress-breakable (progress watermarks): (1) TRIGGERS: a cycle in the wait-for graph; a wait older than [schedule].auto_order_wait_s with nothing running; two or more open items whose globs overlap that repeatedly block each other (an undeclared dependency on a shared file such as a pin file, README.md, help.py). (2) ACTION: choose a deterministic order (priority number, then progress watermark, then claim time, then id) and add `needs` edges from the later items to the earlier ones (only between items that actually collide; transitive reduction applied; NEVER an edge that closes a cycle: re-check with core.graph.find_cycles); the later item's holder is told to yield the contested globs (yield-requested) and cannot reclaim them until the earlier item is done; the earlier item proceeds. (3) LOGGED and REVERSIBLE: each edge is a normal task.updated event by actor ddflow:auto-order with the reason and the evidence (the cycle, the waits), shown in brief and doctor, undone by `ddflow update --needs`; the operator can switch the mode: [schedule].auto_order = off | propose | apply (default apply for a detected cycle or a wait over the limit, propose for repeated collisions), with a per-item opt-out tag no-auto-order. (4) DURABLE: after the same pair collides twice, the edge is kept as a permanent declared dependency so the plan itself is repaired (the edge appears in plan check and the roadmap). (5) SURFACES: ddflow autoorder status|apply|undo on CLI, MCP and prompt. Regression tests: (a) three items with crossing globs produce the edges in the documented order and no cycle; (b) an edge that would create a cycle is refused; (c) propose mode writes nothing; (d) undo restores the old needs. Related: DX-lease-wait-cycle, DX-no-hold-and-wait, DX-lease-progress-breakable, B-gap-plan-lint (plan check), DX-pins-regenerate.

data.title: ddflow orders colliding items itself: a detected circular wait or an undeclared file collision adds needs edges between the items to force an unblock

data.context: Three agents deadlocked for 45+ minutes on 2026-10-15 over shared files (help.py, golden snapshot, setup transcript, README) although no task depended on another.
data.decision: Operator 2026-10-15, verbatim: 'Can you have those DX set for implementation next after the bug fixes and with priority over the other tasks? Can you set the rules, and also can you make sure that ddflow if it detects circular dependency or blockage which was undetected and not prevented in advance should refill the tasks with dependency on each other in order to prevent circular waiting and dependency and this way to force unblock?'. (1) PRIORITY: the locking and ordering features come right after the bug fixes and ahead of every other feature: DX-pins-regenerate, DX-no-hold-and-wait and DX-conflict-autoorder (priority 1), then DX-lease-progress-breakable, DX-lease-wait-cycle and DX-merge-queue (2), then the other DX tasks. (2) PREVENT IN ADVANCE: pin files are regenerated, not leased (DX-pins-regenerate, DX-merge-queue); a lease is never widened by hold-and-wait (DX-no-hold-and-wait); a contended lease without progress is breakable (DX-lease-progress-breakable, D-lease-hold-limit); a task that adds a knob, event kind or command declares the pin files it will touch up front. (3) DETECT: a cycle in the wait-for graph, or a wait older than a limit with nothing running, is reported by doctor, status, brief and the lanes advisor (DX-lease-wait-cycle). (4) SELF-HEAL, the new rule: when ddflow detects a circular dependency or blockage that was NOT declared and NOT prevented in advance, ddflow itself ADDS `needs` edges between the colliding items, in a deterministic order (priority, then progress, then claim time, then id), never an edge that closes a cycle, so the circular waiting cannot recur and the unblock is forced; the later item yields the contested globs and waits for the earlier one. Every edge is a logged event by actor ddflow:auto-order with the evidence, visible in brief and doctor and reversible with ddflow update --needs; [schedule].auto_order = off | propose | apply (default apply for a detected cycle or an over-limit wait, propose for repeated collisions); a repeated collision of the same pair makes the edge permanent in the plan (DX-conflict-autoorder). (5) AGENTS: never poll-wait in a private loop; use ddflow wait or report to the coordinator; do not hold a lease while waiting for another (release or yield on request); when ddflow tells you to yield, do so at the next safe point. Users and companies can change every limit and the mode (r-company-workflows).

data.body:
Today ddflow only LISTS what is ready (`ddflow next` even prints 'These are independent: run them in parallel worktrees') and a person or a master agent must read it, decide, write each agent's brief and start it. 2026-10-15: that coordinator work (checking the cap, picking non-overlapping items, bugs first, writing eight near-identical briefs, noticing idle agents, ordering merges over shared pin files, resuming agents) was done by hand all day and masked this gap. Build the pure planner: given the effective cap (and reserved slots, DX-reserved-slot), running lanes (the lane ledger), ready items from the scheduler, the conflict/overlap and wait graph (DX-no-hold-and-wait), quota/governor guards and the agent groups caps, return the ordered list of items to start NOW (bug fixes first, then priority), each with agent name, claim command, globs, the rendered launch brief (DX-agent-brief) and the pin-file rule; and the lanes to RESUME, YIELD or NUDGE. Idempotent (a second call returns nothing new until state changes). `--tick` writes a dispatch.planned event (what was advised and why) so decisions are auditable. mode advise only: it starts nothing. data.body: Operator question 2026-10-15: if an agent has stopped or its lease was forcefully unlocked, can its work be restored automatically when the blocking part unblocks, or does it need the user? Today: the WORK survives (committed branch, worktree, gate outcomes in the log; cleanup refuses unmerged work; `ddflow recover` lists it) but RESUMING is manual: someone has to notice, recover and `claim --force`, write a new brief, and tell the right agent. On 2026-10-15 the coordinator did this by hand four times (the actors agent, the log-scale agent twice, the docs agent). Build, on the planned resume (P-resume, B-res-resume), the lane ledger (ddflow lanes), the dispatcher (DX-dispatch-plan, DX-dispatch-supervise) and the wait graph (DX-no-hold-and-wait): (1) PARK instead of drop: every way an item loses its lease with work attached (stopped agent, expired lease, yield requested by DX-conflict-autoorder, lease broken by DX-lease-progress-breakable, forced claim) writes a `lane.parked` record: item, branch, worktree, the gates already passed, the last commits, uncommitted diff stat, the REASON, and the RESTORE CONDITION (the item or glob it waits on, a time, or 'operator'); the worktree and branch are protected from cleanup while parked. (2) DERIVED RESUME BRIEF: an agent killed mid-run writes no handoff, so ddflow derives it from the log and the worktree: remaining gates in order, commits ahead of main, files touched, pin files that need re-recording, the last notes and findings, and the exact next commands; if the agent still wrote a handoff (B-am-handoff, P-session-context) it is included. (3) AUTO-WAKE: when the restore condition is met (the blocker merged, the glob is free, the quota window reset) ddflow marks the lane RESUME-READY, moves it AHEAD of fresh items in `ddflow next` (parked work first, priority boost knob), and the dispatcher plan (DX-dispatch-plan) returns a RESUME action with the derived brief: in advise mode the master session is nudged (and told which still-living subagent can simply be sent the brief), in launch mode a lane is started from the worktree. Reclaiming a parked item by its original agent identity or an authorised successor needs no --force. (4) AFTER-RESUME CHECKS: merge main, re-record pins (ddflow pins regenerate), re-run only the gates whose reviewed tree changed, then merge, so a resumed lane does not redo recorded work; a parked item older than a knob is reported to the operator instead of silently waiting. (5) Everything is logged, reversible, and optional per project (`[lane].park`, `[lane].auto_resume` = off | advise | act; default advise); a person can park, resume or discard a lane with ddflow lanes park|resume|discard. Regression tests with fake lanes: a forced unlock parks the lane and keeps its worktree; when the blocker's item completes the lane is RESUME-READY and listed first; the derived brief lists exactly the unfinished gates; discard needs an explicit command. Related: B-res-resume, P-resume, DX-dispatch-supervise, DX-conflict-autoorder, DX-lease-progress-breakable, DX-lapsed-lease-merge-deadlock. data.body:
Operator 2026-10-15 (D-lock-cycle-selfheal): if ddflow detects a circular dependency or blockage that was NOT declared and NOT prevented in advance, it must REFILL the tasks with dependencies on each other so the circular waiting cannot recur, and so force the unblock. Build on DX-lease-wait-cycle (detection: wait-for graph from the waiting_on marks of DX-no-hold-and-wait) and DX-lease-progress-breakable (progress watermarks): (1) TRIGGERS: a cycle in the wait-for graph; a wait older than [schedule].auto_order_wait_s with nothing running; two or more open items whose globs overlap that repeatedly block each other (an undeclared dependency on a shared file such as a pin file, README.md, help.py). (2) ACTION: choose a deterministic order (priority number, then progress watermark, then claim time, then id) and add `needs` edges from the later items to the earlier ones (only between items that actually collide; transitive reduction applied; NEVER an edge that closes a cycle: re-check with core.graph.find_cycles); the later item's holder is told to yield the contested globs (yield-requested) and cannot reclaim them until the earlier item is done; the earlier item proceeds. (3) LOGGED and REVERSIBLE: each edge is a normal task.updated event by actor ddflow:auto-order with the reason and the evidence (the cycle, the waits), shown in brief and doctor, undone by `ddflow update --needs`; the operator can switch the mode: [schedule].auto_order = off | propose | apply (default apply for a detected cycle or a wait over the limit, propose for repeated collisions), with a per-item opt-out tag no-auto-order. (4) DURABLE: after the same pair collides twice, the edge is kept as a permanent declared dependency so the plan itself is repaired (the edge appears in plan check and the roadmap). (5) SURFACES: ddflow autoorder status|apply|undo on CLI, MCP and prompt. Regression tests: (a) three items with crossing globs produce the edges in the documented order and no cycle; (b) an edge that would create a cycle is refused; (c) propose mode writes nothing; (d) undo restores the old needs. Related: DX-lease-wait-cycle, DX-no-hold-and-wait, DX-lease-progress-breakable, B-gap-plan-lint (plan check), DX-pins-regenerate.

D-lease-hold-limit says hot-file locks are visible and time-limited: after hold_max_s a contended lease is breakable. grep finds no hold_max_s in the code (B-lease-hold-visibility, open, only warns). On 2026-10-15 three agents sat for 45+ minutes with current leases because a heartbeat loop renews an idle lease: liveness is not progress. Build: (1) a progress watermark per lease = the last event that is not a lease renewal (a commit, a gate record, a test job start, a note); (2) [lease].hold_max_s and idle_max_s: a lease that another ready item is waiting on (a recorded wait, see DX-lease-wait-cycle) and whose watermark is older than idle_max_s is marked yield-requested in brief/doctor/status, and after hold_max_s it is breakable by the waiter with `ddflow claim --break` (the holder's branch and work are kept; the holder gets the contested globs back only through the normal claim); (3) the holder sees the request in its next ddflow call. Related: B-lease-hold-visibility, DX-lease-wait-cycle. Regression test: an idle lease with a waiter is reported yield-requested and then breakable; an active lease never is.

data.body: Operator 2026-10-15, verbatim: 'Can you also make ddflow to periodically inspect agents and subagents for if they have stalled or locked so it can detect fast situations like these or crashes and to try to correct them'. Today stalls are found only when a person or the coordinator happens to look: on 2026-10-15 one agent sat idle for an hour with a current lease (a heartbeat loop kept renewing it), three agents deadlocked for 45+ minutes, a wait loop timed out unnoticed, and a stopped agent was found by reading event timestamps by hand. Build a WATCHDOG: (1) WHAT IT INSPECTS, per lane (every lease holder, agent and subagent, in the lane ledger): STALLED = no progress for [watch].stall_s while its lease is renewed (progress = the watermark of DX-lease-progress-breakable: the last event that is not a lease renewal, plus commits in its worktree and test jobs in flight); IDLE-HEARTBEAT = renewals continue but nothing else for [watch].idle_s; LOCKED = it is in a cycle of the wait-for graph or waits on a lease held by a stalled lane (DX-lease-wait-cycle); CRASHED = the holder's process or session is gone (lease heartbeats carry pid, host and session id so a dead process is seen in minutes, not after the 30-minute TTL), or its lease expired with work attached; RUNAWAY = the same gate failed N times, the same command repeated, a job over its budget, or a review round loop; UNRESPONSIVE = a nudge or yield request went unanswered for [watch].reply_s; STARVED = context or quota pressure from the governor (P-governor sampling) so the lane cannot continue; and every found condition is a finding with evidence. (2) WHEN, without a daemon (D-sched-no-daemon, amended by D-daemons): opportunistically on every ddflow call, throttled by [watch].interval_s (a cheap check against the last-inspected marker, using the already folded state); in the hook rungs (SessionStart, Stop, SubagentStop, UserPromptSubmit) so the master session sees findings; as a scheduler job (P-schedule due/executor-basic) for headless projects; and, when the operator enables the managed lane-supervisor/scheduler daemon kind (D-daemons), on its tick. (3) CORRECT, as a ladder with a mode per step ([watch].act = off | advise | act, default advise, per finding kind): nudge the lane (a note or message it reads at its next call, P-context-sync.tell / P-spawn.steer); ask for status; request yield of contested globs; PARK the lane (DX-park-and-resume) so its work is kept; take over or relaunch from the worktree (DX-dispatch-supervise); add the ordering edges that stop a recurrence (DX-conflict-autoorder); escalate to the operator with the exact commands. Never discards work, never acts on a lane with progress, every step is a logged event (actor ddflow:watchdog) with its evidence and is reversible. (4) SURFACES: `ddflow watch inspect|status|history|ack` on CLI, MCP and the plain prompt ('is anything stuck?'), a one-line summary in brief, status and the statusline, doctor findings, and the dispatcher plan (DX-dispatch-plan) consumes the same findings so a stalled lane's slot is refilled. (5) Reuse: P-observe.detectors (deterministic detector registry: lock contention, rework loops), the lanes ledger and advisor (`ddflow lanes advise`), the jobs engine for hung test jobs, DX-doctor-ack for acknowledged findings. Regression tests with fake lanes and a fake clock: an idle-heartbeat lane is STALLED after the limit and an active one never; a dead pid is CRASHED within [watch].crash_s; a three-lane crossing-glob case is LOCKED and the ladder escalates step by step; advise mode writes only findings; act mode parks the stalled lane and keeps its worktree; findings are deduplicated and rate-limited. Related: DX-lease-wait-cycle, DX-lease-progress-breakable, DX-no-hold-and-wait, DX-park-and-resume, DX-dispatch-supervise, DX-conflict-autoorder, P-observe.detectors, P-governor.sampling, DX-lapsed-lease-merge-deadlock. CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, r-everything-configurable, r-company-workflows): every limit, mode and interval a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt, per project and org; reuse the shared engines; files under 20 KB.
data.title: A watchdog: ddflow periodically inspects every agent and subagent lane for stalls, locks, crashes and runaways, and corrects them on a ladder

data.body:
What the coordinator did by hand on 2026-10-15: notice that an agent had been idle for an hour holding shared files (events stopped, only heartbeats), stop and replace it, resume stopped agents when their blocker merged, tell waiting agents the merge order, and relaunch finishers. Make it a ddflow function over the lane ledger: stall = no progress watermark (DX-lease-progress-breakable) for [dispatch].stall_s while another item waits; actions in order: nudge the lane, request yield, take over (recover and claim --force for the SAME work when the operator's policy allows), relaunch a stopped lane from its worktree; merge order over shared files via the merge queue (DX-merge-queue); after a merge, tick the planner so freed slots refill; everything is a logged event and each step has a mode (advise, act) and an escalation to the operator. In advise mode it only reports. Regression tests with fake lanes: an idle holder with a waiter is reported and then taken over only when policy allows; a stopped lane with a ready blocker is flagged RESUME; the merge order follows the queue.

Filed 2026-10-15 from the operator's question 'Why is not ddflow automatically filling up the pipelines and parallel agents' (D-file-ddflow-defects). Related, already planned in pieces: P-agent-parity.launcher, P-agent-parity.continuation, CP-backend-iface, P-spawn.engine, P-schedule (executor-basic), P-daemon (lane supervisor kind), P-autopilot, B-adaptive-flow, ddflow lanes (ledger and advisor, done). Decisions in force: D-sched-no-daemon (as amended by D-daemons: ddflow starts nothing unasked), D-agent-parity (launching agents only from operator-set launch templates, with caps and consent), D-daemons (lane supervisor is operator-only), r-lock-cycle-selfheal, D-quotas-governor. CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, r-everything-configurable, r-company-workflows): every number, mode and template a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; per project and per org; reuse the shared engines; files under 20 KB.

AMENDED 2026-10-15: the inspection itself (stalled, locked, crashed, runaway, unresponsive detection and the periodic trigger) is DX-health-watch; this task consumes its findings and does the dispatcher actions (refill, resume, relaunch).

Operator question 2026-10-15: if an agent has stopped or its lease was forcefully unlocked, can its work be restored automatically when the blocking part unblocks, or does it need the user? Today: the WORK survives (committed branch, worktree, gate outcomes in the log; cleanup refuses unmerged work; `ddflow recover` lists it) but RESUMING is manual: someone has to notice, recover and `claim --force`, write a new brief, and tell the right agent. On 2026-10-15 the coordinator did this by hand four times (the actors agent, the log-scale agent twice, the docs agent). Build, on the planned resume (P-resume, B-res-resume), the lane ledger (ddflow lanes), the dispatcher (DX-dispatch-plan, DX-dispatch-supervise) and the wait graph (DX-no-hold-and-wait): (1) PARK instead of drop: every way an item loses its lease with work attached (stopped agent, expired lease, yield requested by DX-conflict-autoorder, lease broken by DX-lease-progress-breakable, forced claim) writes a `lane.parked` record: item, branch, worktree, the gates already passed, the last commits, uncommitted diff stat, the REASON, and the RESTORE CONDITION (the item or glob it waits on, a time, or 'operator'); the worktree and branch are protected from cleanup while parked. (2) DERIVED RESUME BRIEF: an agent killed mid-run writes no handoff, so ddflow derives it from the log and the worktree: remaining gates in order, commits ahead of main, files touched, pin files that need re-recording, the last notes and findings, and the exact next commands; if the agent still wrote a handoff (B-am-handoff, P-session-context) it is included. (3) AUTO-WAKE: when the restore condition is met (the blocker merged, the glob is free, the quota window reset) ddflow marks the lane RESUME-READY, moves it AHEAD of fresh items in `ddflow next` (parked work first, priority boost knob), and the dispatcher plan (DX-dispatch-plan) returns a RESUME action with the derived brief: in advise mode the master session is nudged (and told which still-living subagent can simply be sent the brief), in launch mode a lane is started from the worktree. Reclaiming a parked item by its original agent identity or an authorised successor needs no --force. (4) AFTER-RESUME CHECKS: merge main, re-record pins (ddflow pins regenerate), re-run only the gates whose reviewed tree changed, then merge, so a resumed lane does not redo recorded work; a parked item older than a knob is reported to the operator instead of silently waiting. (5) Everything is logged, reversible, and optional per project (`[lane].park`, `[lane].auto_resume` = off | advise | act; default advise); a person can park, resume or discard a lane with ddflow lanes park|resume|discard. Regression tests with fake lanes: a forced unlock parks the lane and keeps its worktree; when the blocker's item completes the lane is RESUME-READY and listed first; the derived brief lists exactly the unfinished gates; discard needs an explicit command. Related: B-res-resume, P-resume, DX-dispatch-supervise, DX-conflict-autoorder, DX-lease-progress-breakable, DX-lapsed-lease-merge-deadlock. CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, r-everything-configurable, r-company-workflows): every number and mode a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt; reuse the shared engines; files under 20 KB.

AMENDED 2026-10-15: the watchdog (DX-health-watch) is the main producer of park events and the first consumer of a lane's restore condition.

The fix-Bac9d773a44 agent skipped its ci gate because ci had failed on four golden snapshots it could not re-pin (a lease held them), and then merged; main went red (bug B23bd81462d). `gate skip` after a recorded failure turns 'ci failed' into 'ci skipped with a reason', which reads as acceptable. Regression test: skip after a failed ci is refed refused; merge with that state is refused.

data.body: Found by fleet-triagekeep. When main is red for a reason the branch does not touch (B23bd81462d), a gate failure cannot be tied to that cause: gate run and gate record have no way to attach a baseline (this gate fails identically on main at commit X), so complete cannot be unblocked short of --force, which only the operator may grant. Wanted: gate run compares a failure against a fresh run on main and records it as baseline-red with the failing test ids; complete accepts that as evidence, with an explicit reason, and re-runs the gate when main turns green. Related: DX-skip-failed-gate, B23bd81462d.
data.title: Record a gate failure as baseline-red when main fails the same way

data.summary: ddflow gate status B-gap-log-scale crashes with AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get' in ddflow/services/gates/outcomes.py triage_counts (line 88: all(f.get('digest') for f in found)). A gate's evidence chunk_findings holds strings (not dicts), so status, and anything calling _triage_notes, raises a traceback instead of reporting. Other items (SE-ask-core, DX-no-hold-and-wait, fix-Bbba7cecf08) are fine. Likely the evidence-blob offload of chunk_findings on the B-gap-log-scale branch or a hand-recorded gate with a string list. Fix: triage_counts must treat any chunk_findings entry that is not a dict with a digest as 'not triageable' and return None, never raise; add a regression test with a string-list chunk_findings. Risk: the crash can block merge/complete of B-gap-log-scale.
data.title: gate status crashes when chunk_findings holds strings

**Fix**
- `ddflow ci run` and the `ddflow_ci` tool record the item's `ci` gate, with the commit and merge base in the evidence. This happens when the ref is an item id, or when the command is run from a live item's worktree on that tree's own commit.

- The recording code lives in a new module, `ddflow/api/cirun.py`, because importing it from `api/ci.py` creates a circular import and the deferred-import ratchet forbids raising its count. `ci_tool` moved there too.

<result>DX-lease-wait-cycle is merged to main as 9d1a2a18 and completed (event commits 56422773 and 51a21b2d). Every gate has an outcome. The critic and rubber_duck gates passed only on refutation, and the standards and unit_tests gates were recorded against the commit before my last test-only commit.

**What it does**
- **Pure detector:** `ddflow/core/leasewait.py` takes waits and leases and returns the cycles as structured data. `Cycle.as_dict()` is what DX-conflict-autoorder should read.
- **Cycle report:** each cycle names the agents, items, contested files and a victim, plus the globs to drop and the exact `ddflow update`/`release` command. The victim is the youngest wait, because waits carry no progress data until DX-lease-progress-breakable lands.
- **Data source:** `ddflow/api/reporting/waitcycles.py` builds the cycles from the existing `services.waiting` wait-for data. `doctor` reports each cycle as a problem and adds `wait_cycles` to `doctor --json`. `health.py` is at 599 lines, the module-split limit.
- **Knobs:** `loops.wait_cycle` (default true) and `loops.wait_cycle_shown` (default 5), each with an upgrade fragment. I put them in `[loops]` rather than `[lease]` because `config_sections/lease.py` was leased by fleet-leasebreak.

**What it does**
- A lease counts as breakable only if another agent wants its files and it has shown no progress for `hold_max_s`. Progress is any non-lease event on the item (gate outcome, note, job start), a commit on the branch that main lacks, or a changed or deleted file in the worktree. Heartbeats never count.
- The code is in `ddflow/services/leasebreak.py`, `ddflow/infra/treeactivity.py` and `_break_idle` in `ddflow/services/leases.py`.
- Three new knobs under `[lease]`: `idle_max_s` (900), `hold_max_s` (3600) and `break_on_timeout` (default false). Each has an upgrade-manifest fragment, and 0 means off.
- `ddflow claim --break` (CLI and MCP `break`) breaks the lease. A break is all or nothing: if any clashing lease is not breakable, nothing is written.
- A break is recorded as a durable `lease.expired` event carrying `broken_by`, `broken_for`, `idle_s` and `files`, and the holder keeps its worktree and branch.
- The claimant is told in the claim output (`BROKE <item>`). The holder is told in its heartbeat (`BROKEN ...`), and from `idle_max_s` on gets `YIELD REQUESTED`. Brief also shows a "Yield requested" section.
- I moved `_join_line` and `_leave_line` out of `ddflow/api/lifecycle/claim.py` into `claim_line.py`, because `claim.py` would otherwise have passed the 600-line cap.

The changed files are `ddflow/api/surf_setup.py`, `ddflow/surfaces/commands/ci.py` and `tests/test_ci_gate.py`.

**Why it was wrong:** an explicit `--repo` makes the context's start directory the primary, so the foreign-tree check never looked at the shell cwd. The CLI then read the cwd's HEAD directly.

**What it does now:** a new `surf_setup.caller_tree` picks the tree for the default ref:
- **Own tree:** it uses `called_from` when that is a linked worktree. With `--repo`, it uses the cwd when that is a tree of this repo and not another agent's.
- **Foreign tree:** a tree adopted by another identity, or one a different agent works in, falls back to the primary's HEAD.

data.body: Bug B720c59701f: tests/test_lease_progress_breakable.py::test_claim_breaks_a_heartbeat_only_lease_and_tells_both_agents sets lease.idle_max_s=1 and expects the first --break to be refused as fresh; under load the subprocess start exceeds 1 s, so it fails ci (seen 4 times on fix-B0c245a07a1 and likely on others). Fix: use an injected clock (core.clock) or a large idle window with backdated progress instead of real elapsed time; add a test that forces the slow path. Regression test must fail on the unfixed shape.
data.title: Fix bug B720c59701f: flaky lease-break test depends on a 1 s real-time idle window

data.body: Reported by fleet-ciref (and earlier agents). After `ddflow review triage` marks every finding of a failed rubber_duck/critic round refuted, gate status shows 'passed on refutation' in some paths but the gate outcome itself stays failed, so complete refuses and the agent re-records it with `gate record --outcome passed --reviewer-model --reviewed-sha`. Wanted: triage that settles the last open finding of a failed round flips the gate to passed-on-refutation in the log (with the refutation evidence), once, deterministically, and says so; a hand re-record is then unnecessary. Add a test of the whole path: failed round, triage all refuted, gate passes, complete accepts. Related: DX-review-findings-show.
data.title: A review gate stays failed after every finding is triaged refuted; agents re-record it passed by hand

The roadmap is a dependency graph of 978 open tasks in 84 open phases. It has no cycles at task level, and its longest chain is 22 tasks. At phase level it is not a tree: phases depend on each other through different tasks, so the real structure is the task graph grouped into waves. A wave is a set of tasks that can run once all earlier waves are done.

## The trunk
Everything hangs from a few shared tasks. The most waited-on are:

## Waves (how many tasks, what dominates)
| Wave | Tasks | Mostly |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 115 | no prerequisite: agent rules, review budget, backlog items, `P-gaps` |
| 1–2 | 115 + 123 | `P-change-surface`, agent-parity descriptors, test-robustness, doc templates, research, shared engines |

- **Phases that sit deepest:** `P-iac` and `P-app-infra` (waves 14–21), `P-test-domains`, `P-research-flows` and `P-constellation` (12–17).
- **Unplaced tasks:** 22 tasks belong to no phase. `RH-place-unphased` handles them once the move command exists.

Edge direction is fine; clarify that IA-supply-chain only verifies and returns verification results, and AI-artifacts owns the record schema, so the SBOM attach step is AI-artifacts work (or move it). Not a duplicate (verify vs.  (evidence: IA-supply-chain: "an SBOM is attached to the artifact record"; AI-artifacts needs IA-supply-chain.)

<result>fix-B708761957b is merged and completed, and bug B708761957b is closed. One part is not done: the review's call site in `ddflow/api/review.py` still doesn't pass the reviewed tree. The merge commit is 273c7585.

**What changed**
- **Stash dropped from `git_state`:** `ddflow/services/gates/reviewers.py` no longer snapshots the stash list. It is shared by every worktree, and a stash apply, pop or push still changes the index or working tree, so the guard still sees those.
- **Tree argument:** `ddflow/services/review.py` has a new `tree=` argument on `review`, `_race` and `_chat`. The command reviewer is now started in that tree (`cwd=tree`) and watched in it, falling back to the process cwd when none is given. A critic finding showed the tool has to run in the tree it is watched in, so that fix is in too.
- **Other `git_state` readers:** `run_watching_git` is the only other one. It already gets the gate's own directory, so it needed no change.
- **`tests/conftest.py` not edited:** I did not add the autouse chdir. With the stash gone, a sibling worktree can no longer trip the guard. A run from the primary checkout can still see `main` move when a sibling merges. If that flakes again, the chdir is the next step.

**Not done: call-site wiring.** `ddflow/api/review.py` was leased by DX-lease-renew-in-long-commands for the whole run, so I couldn't edit it. Until the api passes the item's tree, real reviews still default to the process cwd. Its `main` HEAD can still move when a sibling merges, which is the leftover exposure above. I filed `DX-review-pass-reviewed-tree` (needs DX-lease-renew-in-long-commands) with the exact change.

**Regression tests** are in `tests/test_reviewer_git_state_scope.py`. Five of them fail on the unfixed code (checked) and pass fixed:

data.body: Operator question 2026-10-16: make review faster but still safe as the code grows. Proposal (needs operator confirmation as a decision, amending D-gate-economy): per-item reviews see only the change's relevant hunks (DX-review-exclude drops generated/pinned files, DX-review-manifest gives each chunk the whole-change manifest) and risk tiers set the depth (tier:fast items get one combined review round, security/engine/hook globs keep the full two-reviewer pipeline; reviewer rules and tier floors are never relaxed: see GV-guardrails). A PHASE-END GLOBAL REVIEW runs as a periodic pass: one cross-family review of the phase's net diff (all merged items) on a large-context reviewer (the 1M-context LAN models), recorded as a periodic pass like integration_tests and required by the phase acceptance task (reuse DX-phase-acceptance-full-suite's hook; knob [review].phase_review = off|require|run). Measured 2026-10-16 (benchmark in /tmp scratch, repeat before deciding): runaway reasoning to the token cap, not diff size, is the main latency on the LAN DeepSeek models, so hedging and smaller chunks stay on.
data.title: Phase-end global review on a large-context reviewer; per-item reviews limited to relevant hunks and risk tiers
